items.title: 'It's not a secret': Inside the town where half the people don't officially exist
items.description: In a community like no other, what happens when people aren't counted? Welcome to the supposedly small country town with hidden houses and five Asian supermarkets.

items.title: Another group of Australians with IS links leave camp in Syria for Australia
items.description: The ABC has seen buses carrying the group, which left the Al Roj camp on Thursday afternoon local time.

items.title: Inside the industrial-scale slave system run by Islamic State
items.description: Australia is the latest country to prosecute its own citizens over Islamic State's system of Yazidi slavery, part of a growing global reckoning over the role some foreign women allegedly played in the atrocities.

items.title: Live: Eleven Australian activists detained by Israel now in Istanbul, minister says
items.description: Social Services Minister Tanya Plibersek says 11 Australian activists who were aboard a flotilla to Gaza and were detained by Israel are in Türkiye. Follow live.

items.title: ASIO cut counterterrorism funding share to post-9/11 low before Bondi
items.description: Australia's intelligence agencies had cut counterterrorism funding to its lowest share this century before the Bondi massacre, despite warnings that a terrorist attack was probable and that antisemitic violence posed an escalating threat to life.

items.title: What we know about Iran's new system of transit in the Strait of Hormuz
items.description: Iran is asserting unprecedented control over the strategically critical waterway, with ships reportedly facing screening processes, transit approvals and potential Bitcoin-backed insurance requirements.

items.title: Cuba on the brink: Residents describe life 'trapped between two psychopaths'
items.description: As power and petrol supplies run out, Cubans tell the ABC about their daily lives. "You can no longer find streets packed with travellers, music and dance," one says. "Only Cuban nationals, still attempting to take some bread home."

items.title: Live: ASX to climb, oil drops on US–Iran deal hopes
items.description: Australian markets are set to rise this morning, as oil falls on hopes of a diplomatic way out of the war in Iran. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Snowy bosses paid $1.2m in bonuses as hydro project costs spiral
items.description: The renewables project's chief executive, Dennis Barnes, received $323,000 in bonus pay on top of his $1.69 million salary last financial year, while four other senior executives received about $919,000 in "variable pay".

items.title: Chalmers asked to explain how he 'landed on 30 per cent' tax rate
items.description: The Productivity Commission was not asked to model how changes to capital gains tax would impact Australia's economy. Business groups say Treasurer Jim Chalmers must explain how the government concluded its tax changes would ultimately be a boon to productivity.

items.title: Half Australia's farms are in trusts. So what does tax reform mean for farmers?
items.description: Despite winning a carve-out to changes to family trusts announced in the budget, farmers are still worried about what tax reform means for them.

items.title: 'Is that a UFO?' Suspected meteor lights up skies across NSW
items.description: Colourful streaks across the skies have been spotted from Bondi to Canberra as a "fireball" meteor passed through the atmosphere overnight.

items.title: Parents of children in foster care say 'black eyes' and bite marks were ignored
items.description: The parents of two children in Northern Territory foster care have spoken out about their "heartbreaking" experience with the system, saying concerns their daughter was being abused by her foster family were brushed off by the department.

items.title: In 1990 there were 599 million mental disorder cases globally. Now there are 1.2 billion
items.description: A surge over the last three decades means mental disorders now account for more than 17 per cent of all disability worldwide, according to a report published this week.

items.title: The Mushroom Tapes, Mad Mabel and Memorial Days triumph at book awards
items.description: In May 2025, Helen Garner, Chloe Hooper and Sarah Krasnostein, three literary true-crime writers, headed to Erin Patterson's trial. The resulting book just won an Australian Book Industry Award.

items.title: The hidden codes and Aussie influence in Harry Connick Jr's new symphony
items.description: Harry Connick Jr's new symphony, Elaboratio, is filled with musical tributes to his mother Anita. Orchestra Victoria and Australian conductor Jessica Gethin are bringing those memories to life at Carnegie Hall.

items.title: Friday news quiz: A pumped prince, a grinning sculpture and a stowaway frog
items.description: You'll be as happy as Prince William when you take this week's quiz, which goes off like a frog in a … bag of lettuce.

items.title: Sydney council to rollout fees to use dozens of public parks
items.description: A picnic vendor told the ABC they found out about the proposed fees through a group chat with other small businesses, and fears the proposed fee structure could "kill an entire industry".

items.title: Soft plastics industry at breaking point, as waste instead sent overseas
items.description: The soft plastic recycling industry wants more waste to stay here, saying too much material is being sent overseas.

items.title: US-bound plane diverted after passenger from Ebola-hit Congo boards 'in error'
items.description: The US has introduced new restrictions on travellers from countries exposed to an Ebola outbreak in Africa, requiring them to enter through Washington DC.

items.title: Air France and Airbus fined for 2009 crash that killed 228
items.description: France's national airline Air France and Airbus have both been found guilty of involuntary manslaughter over a 2009 crash that killed 228 people.

items.title: UK trade staff told to be 'careful and sometimes strict' in dealing with Andrew
items.description: The historic documents show no security vetting took place at the time.

items.title: Dismay, anger over 1870s mansion reduced to rubble
items.description: How did a colonial-era mansion once earmarked to be on the state heritage register get bulldozed?

items.title: 'Absolute shock': NASCAR champion Kyle Busch dies aged 41
items.description: Kyle Busch, who won two Cup Series championships and will be a future NASCAR Hall of Famer, has died aged 41.

items.title: What is 'pink slime' journalism and has it infiltrated Australian media?
items.description: Experts say a series of AI-generated digital news outlets is the first recorded example of "pink slime" journalism in Australia, with the website owner claiming the now-deleted outlets were an experiment gone wrong.
